title: Property damage · loss adjuster site visit
subtitle: Required inspection record
source: Synthetic. Derived from published property-claim inspection standards. Not any insurer's form.

items.prompt: Date and time the damage was first discovered
items.guidance: A sufficient answer records a date, and either a time or a part of the day. 'A few weeks back' or 'recently' is not sufficient.

items.prompt: Cause of loss as described by the policyholder
items.guidance: A sufficient answer records what the policyholder believes caused the damage and what they observed. 'It just happened' is not sufficient. Record the account given; do not assess whether it is plausible.

items.prompt: Whether the escape of water has been isolated, and by whom
items.guidance: A sufficient answer records whether the leak is stopped and who stopped it — the policyholder, a plumber, or nobody yet.

items.prompt: Rooms affected and the extent in each
items.guidance: A sufficient answer names each affected room and describes what is damaged in it. 'Downstairs is a mess' is not sufficient.

A sufficient answer records whether floors, walls, ceilings or joists are affected, and where. This item carries a structural-safety implication: record the observation only and do not offer a suggested wording.

items.prompt: Contents damaged, with approximate age and condition before the loss
items.guidance: A sufficient answer lists the damaged contents and gives approximate age or condition for each. A bare list with no age or condition is not sufficient.

items.prompt: Steps taken to prevent further damage
items.guidance: A sufficient answer records what was done, by whom, and roughly when. 'We sorted it' is not sufficient.

A sufficient answer records whether the property is currently lived in and which facilities are unusable. Offer no suggested wording: habitability drives an alternative-accommodation decision and must be the adjuster's own words.

A sufficient answer records previous claims with approximate dates, or a clear statement that there are none. A formal decline is a valid resolution and must be recorded as declined, not as an answer.
A sufficient answer records what has been photographed, by room or by item. 'Got some pictures' is not sufficient.
